note: Hand-verified expectations, one row per word (SPEC Principle 5, 2026-09-05). Each row is a fact read off the extracts at kaikki 2026-09-01 and the curation tables, never a hope: kind is morphs, decomposed, single, rowonly or none; parts are the ordered chip forms as the card shows them. The build scores itself against these rows on every run and fails under the score in gold-score.json. A field report becomes a row here before it becomes a fix.

rows.why: bor+ la componens; compōnēns is a participle page stepping to compōnō, whose ety reads con- + pōnō
bor la-med manūscrīptum, an inflection of manūscrīptus, whose prose reads manu (ablative of manus) + scriptus (past participle of scribere)
der la absolūtus, the participle of absolvō, whose etymon reads ab- + solvō

der la absolūtiōnem, an inflection of absolūtiō = absolvō + -tiō; absolute attaches to absolvō and absolution reaches it as a part, so it is an anchor under the 2026-09-05 reach rule (review finding 4) and its card carries ab- + solvō
der la pressāre, the infinitive of pressō, whose ety reads premō + -tō
der la impressus, the participle of imprimō, whose etymon reads in- + premō
der grc σύστημα = σῠνῐ́στημῐ + -μᾰ (length marks stripped); συνίστημι = συν- + ἵστημι and is no anchor
der grc περίοδος; the Greek page splits it as περῐ́ + ὁδός, the preposition περί through the length-mark rule
bor+ la idea, der grc ἰδέα: the deepest run is Greek and ἰδέα has no split (its etymon names one parent)
der la soccus, der grc σύκχος: σύκχος is an alternative-form page, no node, so the Latin run is the deepest that exists
der la cūriōsus; the Latin page records a back-formation from incūriōsus, and SOURCE_SPLITS carries the standard analysis cūra + -ōsus
der la dēpōnēns steps to dēpōnō (LEMMA_STEPS and the participle step agree), whose ety reads dē- + pōnō
bor la haesitātiōnem steps to haesitātiō = haesitō + -tiō; haesitō is an anchor (hesitance and hesitation both reach it) and carries haereō + -titō on its card
der la accessus, whose noun entry reads accēdō + -tus; accēdō is an anchor
der la concēdō, whose ety reads con- + cēdō
der la territōrium = terra + -tōrium
der la-lat rememorari steps to rememoror, which ROOT_ALIASES folds onto la:memor; the page says only From memoror
der la memoria = memor + -ia
FORCED_SPLITS; the extract analyses it as Latin subterrāneus + -an
af en Korea + -an; Korea is a proper noun with no card, so its chip is inert
inh enm sky, der non ský (cloud): the deepest attested origin is Old Norse, a row-only language
der la cava (cavity); the page has a hollow noun and a jackdaw noun, and the attaching gloss picks the hollow
inh ang piper, der la piper: the Latin run is the deepest root language and piper has no split
der la mea domina, a two-word lemma Wiktionary never wrote; the misses report says so
inh enm knowen, inh ang cnāwan; Latin cognoscō sits only in a cog template under the Cognates heading, so no classical row (review finding 1)
inh enm riden, inh ang rīdan; Greek ὀρίνω is a cog template in the cognate list, so no classical row (review finding 1)
inh enm streight, der ang streċċan; Latin strictus is a noncog mention in the conflation note about strait, so no classical row (review finding 1)
der la iūstus; the Latin page reads surf iūs + -tus, and the iūs card follows the law entry: justice glosses iūs as right, just as law, right (review finding 2)
der la computō = con- + putō; the putō page has one lemma entry, so the chip names it whatever the card gloss says (review finding 2)
der la collēgium = collēga + -ium; collēga is an anchor carrying con- + legō, and the legō card follows the gather entry (review finding 2)
der la collecta, whose page steps through collēctus to colligō = com- + legō (to gather), flattened to the page's own parts (review finding 2)
der la-lat lectura, der la lectus (past participle of legō): the run settles on legō, whose gather entry has no split (review finding 2)
der la dēcīdere, infinitive of dēcīdō (cut off, decide), from dē + caedō: the page dēcidō has two entries and the cut entry wins on the form, the gloss and the named part (review finding 3)
der la accidēns, participle of accidō (happen) = ad + cadō: the fall entry of accido wins on the gloss and the named part cadō (review finding 3)
der la-lat captio with the verb form captiāre, a page whose only entry is the noun deception, so it is skipped; der la captō = capiō + -tō (review finding 3)
der la fundō with the form fundāre, the first-conjugation entry (to found) = fundus + -ō; the pour entry is fundere (review finding 3)
der la situs (position, place, site): the noun entry = sinō + -tus wins on the gloss over the participle (review finding 3)

der la impāctus: the noun entry (collision, hit) = impingō + -tus wins on the first definition (collision) (review finding 3); impinge attaches to impingō and impact reaches it as a part, so it is an anchor under the 2026-09-05 reach rule (review finding 4) and its card carries in- + pangō
der la liquor (fluidity, liquidness): the noun entry = liqueō + -or wins on the gloss over the deponent verb (review finding 3)
der grc αὐτόματον; the English page writes "from αὐτός + μέμαα" for it, and αὐτός is an anchor (auto- words reach it), so it stays whole with its card carrying αὖ + ὁ (review finding 4)
der LL. idemptitās,identitās (the first form fails, the alternative resolves) with the chain idem + -tās; the Greek ταὐτότης on the page is a calque and rejected (review findings 1 and 4)
der la-lat ossuārium; the Latin page reads from ossua (ossa, os) + -ārius, and the trailing ", alternative form of os" no longer steps -ārius to os (review finding 4)
der la iūstitia = iūstus + -itia; just attaches to iūstus and justice reaches it, so it is an anchor and the row stops there (review finding 4)
der grc ἐνέργεια = ἐνεργής + -ιᾰ with ἐνεργής = ἐνεργός + -ης; the full expansion ran to five chips, so ἐνεργός stays whole and its card carries ἐν- + ἔργον + -ος (review finding 4)
der la deportāre with {{pre|la|de-|portāre}} written after it: the template's parts belong to dēportō, the term named before its expansion (review finding 5)
der la-ecc persecutor, der la persequor with {{prefix|la|per|sequor}} after it: the parts belong to persequor, and its page reads per- + sequor (review finding 5)
uder la funereus with "+ -al" from {{suffix|en|3=al}}: the English suffix comes off the chain, and fūnereus reads fūnus + -eus (review finding 5)
bor hi आरती, der sa आरात्रिक: the deepest term is Sanskrit, a row-only language; the rom ārātrika comes from the expansion (review finding 6)
der sa अवतार (descent of a deity from a heaven); rom avatāra from the expansion (review finding 6)
bor ru большеви́к; rom bolʹševík from the expansion (review finding 6)
der ar قُطُن, from der he כֻּתֹּנֶת: Hebrew is the deepest; its rom kuttṓnĕṯ sits in the prose after the expansion (review finding 6)
inh enm scope, der dum scoep and der dum schoppe with no step cue between (alternatives; the first is shown); Dutch schop is a cog template (review finding 7)
inh enm swam, inh ang swamm, then Proto-West Germanic *swamm ends the walk; Dutch zwamp is a cog template (review finding 7)
inh enm crike, der non kriki, then Proto-Germanic *krikjô ends the walk; Middle Dutch krēke is a reborrowing aside later in the sentence (review finding 7)
inh enm advaunte-garde,avauntgard: the first form of the comma-joined list; Old French is pass-through with nothing deeper (review finding 7)
bor frm cosaque, der zlw-mpl Kozak, der otk 𐰴𐰔𐰍𐰸 (profiteer): Old Turkic, a code under the census threshold, is the deepest attested term (review finding 7)
bor hi गोरा / bor ur گورا are alternatives (the first is shown); Pahari-Potwari and Punjabi follow "influenced also by" and are asides (review finding 7)
der de Steppe or der fr steppe, in turn from der ru степь (flat grassy plain) or der uk степ: Russian is the deepest step, Ukrainian its alternative (review finding 7)
bor fr corridor, der it corridore (long passage): the page's own deepest term, read before the walked French page (review finding 7)
bor pt manga, from der ml മാങ്ങ / der ta மாங்காய், possibly via der ms mangga: Malayalam first, Tamil an alternative, Malay a via stage (review finding 7)
der grc ἀνθόλοψ; the Greek page carries {{unk}} and calls ἄνθος + ὤψ a superficial resemblance and a corruption, so the af template's split is refused (review finding 8)
der grc σκίουρος; the Greek page says the σκιά + οὐρά reading could be a folk etymology, and the English page's repeat of it is not shown (review finding 8)
der grc λύσσα; the Greek page carries {{unc|grc|disputedly}}, so its λύκος + -ια split is refused, and a tail word needs a decomposed row to ship (review finding 8)
bor frm race from der it razza, of uncertain origin, with a theories list below: the page's own statement stands and the French page's Latin generātiō is not walked (review findings 1 and 8)
inh enm Tewesday, inh ang tīwesdæġ (Tuesday), then Proto-West Germanic ends the walk; Latin diēs Mārtis is a cog template after "interpretation of" (review finding 8)
inh enm Wednesday, inh ang *wēdnesdæġ (unattested); Latin diēs Mercuriī follows "a calque of" and is rejected (review finding 8)
der la quālitās; the Latin page reads "Coined by Cicero as a calque of Ancient Greek ποιότης, from quālis + -tās": the calque cue names the model and the chain resumes at from (review finding 8)
der la mediocris with {{af|la|medius|ocris}} inside its parenthesis: the Latin term is located by its term when its expansion is not in the prose, and owns the parts (review finding 5)
der la-lat advisō, no page, with the etymon tree's ad- + visō under it: the unwritten lemma labels the row over the parts the tree gives it (review finding 5)
der la cohaesus, past participle of cohaereō, + -ive: the English suffix comes off the chain and cohaesus steps to cohaereō = con- + haereō (review finding 5)
der la pāgānus = pāgus + -ānus; the Greek ἄγροικος later on the page sits in a "Note the opposition" sentence and is an aside (review finding 8)
